fieldNotes.title: Field Notes: 100 articles, ranking gone in 21 days
fieldNotes.source: Anonymous SEO consultant at a Mumbai content agency
fieldNotes.story:
Client asked us to publish 100 articles in 7 days. Brief: 'use AI to scale.' We did. 100 AI-drafted, lightly-edited blog posts went live across two weeks.

Week 3 of week-3: Google's spam-content update hit. **Domain authority dropped from 47 to 11.** 73 of the 100 articles got de-indexed. Organic traffic fell 84%. Client lost ~₹30 lakh in pipeline that quarter.

The 27 surviving articles? They were the ones we had a writer rewrite top-to-bottom — i.e., the ones where AI was a starter draft, not the shipped artifact. The agency kept the client by spending Q4 doing content cleanup: deleting 73, rebuilding 47 with full human craft. We charged the client extra. Could have charged less and shipped 12 great articles to begin with.
fieldNotes.takeaway: AI-as-shipped-artifact loses to AI-as-draft + human craft. Volume is a vanity metric; rankings live or die on craft.

bossBattle.title: Boss Battle: 100 articles or 12?
bossBattle.setup: Sneha's content lead pitches: '100 AI-drafted articles per month for ₹47K — agency-quality, SEO-tuned.' Founder loves the numbers. Sneha's been burned before. She has to call it.

stages.prompt: Founder pitches the 100/month plan. What's Sneha's first move?

options.label: Counter-propose: 12 great articles per month (AI-drafted, human-crafted to ship), at ₹38K. Same budget, 1/8 volume, far higher craft.
options.explain: Right. Volume is the vanity; craft is the asset. Re-frame the budget around outcome, not output count.

options.label: Approve the 100 plan; ship at scale.
options.explain: Same Mumbai agency story plays out. Ranking risk is unbounded.

options.label: Reject content entirely.
options.explain: Overcorrection. Content with craft is still leverage; just not at 100/month volumes.

stages.prompt: Founder asks: 'why won't the 100/month work? Other brands are doing it.'

options.label: Show the Google spam-content update + 3 case studies of de-indexing. Pin to: 'volume is a leading indicator of penalty, not growth.'
'Trust me, 100 is bad.'
options.explain: Founder doesn't update on assertion. Need evidence.

options.label: 'Other brands are wrong.'
options.explain: Doesn't help. Frame the risk in $ and rankings, not opinions.

options.label: Brief (with brand voice anchor) → AI draft → human structure edit → human voice edit → SEO review → ship. 5 stages.
options.explain: Right. Each stage adds craft. The brand voice anchor is what AI cannot replicate without 3 sample posts.

options.label: AI draft → ship.
options.explain: Same de-indexing risk; just 12 articles instead of 100.

options.label: AI draft → quick proofread → ship.
options.explain: Single human gate insufficient. Three gates (structure, voice, SEO) is the discipline.

outcomes.perfect: S-tier. Sneha ships 12 great articles in month 1; ranking moves up; founder reframes 'AI for content scale' to 'AI for content craft'. Q2 budget renewed.
outcomes.good: 12 articles shipped; rankings stable. One article got rejected mid-pipeline (off-brand). Worth the friction.
outcomes.learn: Re-read the de-indexing case. Volume without craft is a ranking risk, not an asset.
